title: Schema stub bridge for Python SDK: lightweight runtime models, lazy hydration, and retry-aware streaming
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Our Python SDK currently forces full deserialization into heavy pydantic/dataclass objects for streaming LLM responses and structured outputs. For long-lived streams (chat/assistant sessions) and high-concurrency workloads this increases memory pressure and latency during retries.

Goal: Provide a lightweight, runtime-generated 'schema stub' bridge that: (1) represents typed response shapes with minimal allocation during streaming, (2) defers full hydration into pydantic/dataclass objects until the consumer explicitly requests it, and (3) exposes explicit retry/idempotency markers and partial-checkpoint helpers for safe stream resume and replay. The feature should be backwards-compatible with existing SDK ergonomics and offer clear migration guidance and examples.
acceptance_criteria: Provide a runtime schema-stub generator that emits minimal Python objects (stubs) for response chunks with typed attribute access but without pydantic validation overhead
Support both dataclass-first and pydantic-first consumers via a stable .hydrate() API that eagerly converts a stub to the requested target model
Streaming memory usage decreases by >= 35% on the representative chat benchmark (10 concurrent streams, 512 token average) compared to current baseline
Retry-safe streaming semantics: stubs carry a stream_token and idempotency_key; resuming a stream can rehydrate from last checkpoint without duplicating side-effects
Comprehensive unit + integration tests and an end-to-end example notebook demonstrating lazy hydration, retries, and a canary rollout
Documentation, migration guide, and code samples included in SDK docs and the quickstart repo
implementation_notes: RFC: runtime generator builds thin stub classes using types.SimpleNamespace + __slots__ for predictable memory layout
Hydration API: stub_obj.hydrate(target='pydantic'|'dataclass'|'native') which triggers validation only on demand
Backpressure/redelivery: when a retry occurs, the runtime will re-emit previously produced stub objects with the same stream_token; consumers can opt into dedupe by comparing idempotency_key
Validation strategy: lightweight structural checks on the stub (presence of required fields) during streaming; full validation deferred to hydrate()
Compatibility: provide automatic adapters for existing typed helpers (hydrators) and a shim layer for older SDK versions
Performance: use a pooled string intern cache for common keys and reuse small tuple containers for leaf sequences to reduce GC churn
Edge cases: streaming partial unions (oneOf) will emit a minimal discriminant field on the stub to let consumers decide when to hydrate
Telemetry: add metric sdk.stub.hydrate.latency and sdk.stub.allocation.bytes; include sample dashboard link in Related Links
qa_plan: Unit tests: stub construction, attribute access, hydrate() permutations, validation failures
Integration tests: streaming client server harness with network jitter; assert memory and latency targets
Fuzzing: generate malformed chunks to validate graceful degradation and error messages
Canary: enable feature flag for 5% of SDK traffic and monitor sdk.stub.hydrate.latency and error_rate
Rollback: feature toggle to revert to legacy hydration path; run rollback-validation job
